open-question.question: Should the complete-all-tasks orchestrator keep committing the agent-staged index with its own git commit line behind its own nothing-staged guard, only changing the subject and dropping the body, or should its commit be routed through the shared commit procedure (which guards on PATHS the orchestrator does not know) by giving that procedure a staged-index mode?
open-question.alternative: Leave step 2c of `core/skills/complete-all-tasks/SKILL.md` as it is: the orchestrator keeps its own `git diff --cached --quiet` nothing-staged guard and its own `git commit` with no pathspec. The only changes are that the subject becomes `Task-completion: <TASK_NAME>`, reusing the heading step 2b already holds, and the `-m "<body>"` argument and the heading-in-body sentence are removed. This is the smallest change that meets the goal. It touches one step of one skill, leaves `core/shared/commit-procedure.md` and all of its roughly seventeen other callers alone, and keeps the arrangement CLAUDE.md already records: the agent stages, the orchestrator commits the index behind a nothing-staged guard, with no `--allow-empty`. The milestone stays a subject-and-docs change. The two completion runners still commit by two different routes. The inline skill goes through the shared procedure and the orchestrator uses its own hand-written guard and commit line. The subjects will match, but a future change to commit mechanics, such as a new flag or trailer, has to be made in two places, and nothing keeps them in step.

Give `core/shared/commit-procedure.md` a second, staged-index mode, chosen when the caller supplies no PATHS and states that the index is already staged. In that mode the procedure guards on `git diff --cached --quiet`, skips its staging step, and commits the index as it stands under SUBJECT, with or without BODY. Step 2c of the orchestrator is rewritten to hand the procedure only the subject `Task-completion: <TASK_NAME>`, the same way the inline `complete-task` skill does. Every skill-layer commit in the plugin then goes through the one shared procedure. That fits CLAUDE.md's rule that commit mechanics live only in `core/shared/commit-procedure.md`, and it means the two completion runners differ only in what they supply, not in how they commit. A procedure every committing skill loads gets a second branch that only one caller uses. Its PATHS-first contract becomes conditional: it stages exactly the named paths, unless there are none, in which case it commits whatever the index holds. That weakens the "a dirty tree elsewhere cannot contaminate this commit" guarantee for anyone who reads the procedure. The change also reaches beyond this milestone's stated scope (the subject, the docs, and the rebuilt hosts), and the CLAUDE.md committing invariant has to be restated to match.

Leave the shared procedure unchanged. At commit time the orchestrator lists the agent-staged files with `git diff --cached --name-only` and passes that list to `core/shared/commit-procedure.md` as PATHS, along with the new subject. Both runners use the shared procedure word for word and its text stays untouched. The orchestrator's hand-written guard and commit line go away without a new mode in the procedure. It breaks the procedure's input contract, which requires PATHS to be decided "without content inspection" and never found by diffing the tree. The procedure's `git add <PATHS>` would also re-stage the whole working-tree state of those files. That could sweep in unstaged hunks the agent deliberately left out, so the commit would stop being exactly the change set the agent staged.

Extend the dispatched `core/agents/complete-task.md` agent so that, on success, it reports the paths it staged along with its DONE token. The orchestrator then passes those paths as PATHS to the unchanged shared commit procedure, and step 2c's own guard and commit line are deleted. The shared procedure gets the input it was designed for, a caller-known set of paths, so both completion runners commit through it with no change to its contract and no looking at the tree. It changes a dispatched agent's return contract. CLAUDE.md records that `complete-all-tasks` keeps a last-line token and that "the agent hands back nothing to collect". The orchestrator would then need to parse and trust a list of paths, which brings back the problem of judging an unreliable return that the alternatives orchestrator needed a whole repair pipeline to handle. Re-staging the reported paths also runs the same risk of sweeping in unstaged hunks, and all of this is far outside this milestone's subject-only goal.
open-question.recommendation: The Goal is a subject-and-docs change, and the orchestrator already holds the heading it needs; every other route rewrites the shared procedure's PATHS-first contract or the agent's return contract, widening the milestone to fix a two-line duplication that CLAUDE.md already records as the intended arrangement.

open-question.question: The ask-in-milestone-context skill states that the task-to-commit mapping is best-effort and not keyed on the heading in the subject line; once every completion subject carries the heading verbatim, should that sentence be rewritten to say the mapping is keyed on the heading for commits made after this change, or left as-is because older history stays unkeyed?
open-question.alternative: Rewrite the step 2 sentence in `core/skills/ask-in-milestone-context/SKILL.md` (line 54) to say two things. Task-completion commits made from now on are keyed on the task's `##` heading in the `Task-completion:` subject. Older history maps only best-effort, because the 218 `Tasklist-completion: complete one milestone task` commits put the heading in the body. Git stays a supporting lens under the existing "never the sole source" rule. It is the most accurate account of what the runner will actually find. The runner is told that a `git log --grep` on the subject is reliable for new work, and why older milestones behave differently, in this repository and in every consuming project that already has orchestrator history. The runtime skill now describes the history of a retired commit format. That cuts against the rule that runtime files hold only what the runner needs and name no retired mechanics. The sentence also goes stale again if the subject format ever changes. Headings are unique only within a milestone, and later fix-up commits carry no marker, so even the "keyed" half is keyed only within a milestone.

Rewrite the sentence so it tells the runner to look for the task's heading text in completion commits, checking both subject and body, without naming either marker or either era. For example: completion commits carry the task heading, so a heading search usually finds the commit, but the mapping stays best-effort. Keep the fall-back to reading the live files. One instruction covers both new subjects and the old heading-in-body commits. A body-inclusive `git log --grep` matches both. The sentence becomes true for all history, not just future commits, and the retired `Tasklist-completion:` format never has to appear in runtime prose. It is less precise than the era-scoped wording. The runner is not told that the subject alone is authoritative for new commits, so it may run a broader, noisier search than it needs to. It also relies on old bodies holding the bare heading, which is true of the orchestrator's past commits but is not stated anywhere the runner can check.

Make the smallest possible edit: delete "not keyed on the heading in the subject line" and keep "the task→commit mapping is best-effort" and everything else in the bullet. The skill then makes no claim either way about subject keying. It removes the only statement the change makes false, as the milestone's starting state notes. It adds no new claim that could itself go stale, and it keeps the bullet's framing of git as a supporting lens. The edit is one clause in one runtime file, plus the rebuilt `hosts/` copies. The runner loses a useful hint. New completion commits are now directly findable by heading in the subject, but the skill no longer says so. The runner will still treat the mapping as unreliable and may skip a cheap, exact lookup it could have used.

Leave line 54 as it is, on the reasoning that most existing history (218 of 221 completion commits) stays unkeyed in the subject. Under that reading, "best-effort, not keyed on the heading in the subject line" is still true of the history as a whole. Nothing changes, and the milestone stays limited to the two runners and the docs its Goal names. The sentence's practical advice (use git to enrich, never as the sole source, fall back to live files) is still sound whatever the subject format. For every commit made after this change the sentence is literally false, and the starting state already flags it as a claim "that becomes false". The runtime would keep a known-inaccurate statement about the very convention this milestone introduces, and the runner would be steered away from the one lookup the change makes reliable.
open-question.recommendation: A heading search over subject and body is true of all history, old and new, in this repository and in consuming projects; it gives the runner the cheap lookup the change makes reliable while naming no marker or retired format, which the era-scoped wording would put into a runtime file and the clause-only deletion would withhold.

open-question.question: Should the CLAUDE.md committing invariant record the unified Task-completion subject and name the retired Tasklist-completion marker as something a later editor must not restore, or is the runtime and docs change enough with no CLAUDE.md edit?
open-question.alternative: Leave `CLAUDE.md` as it is. The milestone changes only the runtime files, `docs/skill-reference.md`, `docs/workflow.md`, and the rebuilt `hosts/` trees. The committing invariant at line 95 already says every skill commits under a function-derived `<Marker>: <descriptor>` subject, and it names no completion subject at all. It follows the rule that only rationale lives in `CLAUDE.md` and the mechanics live in the runtime files. It adds no new copy of a literal subject string that could drift. Nothing in line 95 becomes false, because the bullet names neither `Tasklist-completion:` nor `Task-completion:`. Unifying the subject is also not a surprising design choice that a later editor would be tempted to undo. Nothing warns a later editor against bringing back a separate orchestrator marker with the heading in the body. The old pattern will still look like precedent: 218 commits in history use it, and the ledgers of milestones 14, 15, 16, 18, 25, and 29 quote it. This option is also only complete if the orchestrator's own commit line and nothing-staged guard survive. If that commit is instead routed through the shared commit procedure, line 95's `complete-all-tasks` clause goes stale and needs editing anyway.

Extend the committing bullet at line 95 with one clause. It says that both completion runners commit subject-only under `Task-completion: <Task Title>`, with the task's `##` heading copied exactly. It also says the retired `Tasklist-completion:` marker, with its heading-in-body commits, must not be restored. Each point gets its rationale: one subject for one unit of work whichever runner makes it, and the heading visible in the subject line so history can be searched without reading commit bodies. It matches how `CLAUDE.md` already guards against regressions. Retired designs are named with the reason they must not come back, as in "The old role-based commit split is retired" and the retired recommendation commit and sentinel entries. So a later editor who finds the old marker in history or in the ledgers can see that it was deliberately replaced, and why. It puts a literal subject format into an invariants file that says mechanics belong in the runtime files. That makes one more place to keep in sync with the two SKILL.md files and the docs. It also makes an already long bullet longer.

Append only a short retirement note to line 95, in the style of "The old role-based commit split is retired". It would say that the separate `Tasklist-completion:` marker is retired and both completion runners share one subject. The literal `Task-completion: <Task Title>` format stays in the runtime files and docs. It guards against the regression while copying no subject format into `CLAUDE.md`. That keeps the edit small and keeps mechanics out of the invariants file. A bare retirement note without the reason gives a later editor little to weigh. They may not see why a per-runner marker is wrong, so the guard is weaker than one that states the rationale. It still adds a marker name to `CLAUDE.md` that must stay accurate.

Give no task in this milestone a `CLAUDE.md` edit. Leave it to `/finish-current-milestone` to decide at step 7 whether the unified subject counts as a lasting change to how the project works. It keeps this milestone's scope to the runtime files, the docs, and `hosts/`. The `CLAUDE.md` judgment is made once, when the final shape of the orchestrator's commit is known, rather than now. Step 7's job is environment context, meaning new tools, conventions, and documentation locations. It is not recording invariants, so it may reasonably skip the change and leave `CLAUDE.md` silent by default. This question also stays open instead of being recorded in `## Decisions`, so whether `CLAUDE.md` changes rests on a later pass's discretion rather than a decision made here.
open-question.recommendation: The regression risk is real, since 218 commits and six milestone ledgers make the old marker look like precedent, and CLAUDE.md already guards retired designs by naming them with their reason; a bare retirement note gives a later editor nothing to weigh, and deferring to the finish step leaves an invariant to a pass whose job is environment context.

open-question.question: The How skills commit paragraph in docs/workflow.md says complete-all-tasks commits once per task without naming its subject; should it be extended to state that both completion runners share the Task-completion subject with the heading, or left unchanged since it is not made false by the change?
open-question.alternative: In the `## How skills commit` paragraph of docs/workflow.md, extend "`/complete-all-tasks` commits once per task" to name its subject: `Task-completion: <task heading>` with no body, the same subject inline `/complete-task` uses. The same paragraph already names the subject and body of each of the other four batch skills (`Recommendation-answer: <Short Title>` with the lifted line as body, `Alternatives-annotation: <Short Title>` with no body, and so on), so `/complete-all-tasks` is currently the only batch skill there without one. Naming it makes the paragraph consistent and puts the milestone's main claim, one shared subject for both completion runners, into the narrative doc. The Goal lists docs/workflow.md among the docs to bring into line, and this makes it do so explicitly. It adds a third place where the subject is spelled out, besides the two runtime SKILL.md files and docs/skill-reference.md. A later change to the subject then has one more sentence to keep in sync. It also makes a paragraph that is already very long a little longer.

Leave the docs/workflow.md paragraph as it is. It already lists `Task-completion:` among the example markers and says only that `/complete-all-tasks` commits once per task, and the change makes neither statement false. No edit, and no extra copy of the subject to keep in sync. docs/skill-reference.md, which the milestone edits anyway, remains the one place that states each runner's subject, and the workflow doc stays at narrative level. `/complete-all-tasks` remains the only batch skill in that paragraph whose subject goes unnamed. A reader has to go to docs/skill-reference.md to learn that it now shares `Task-completion:` with `/complete-task`. Since the Goal names docs/workflow.md as a doc to bring into line, leaving it untouched means that part of the Goal is met only because nothing in the file became wrong, not because the file was updated.
open-question.recommendation: The paragraph names the subject and body of every other batch skill, so the orchestrator is the one gap, and the Goal lists docs/workflow.md among the docs to bring into line; one clause makes that explicit at the cost of a sentence that changes only if the subject does.
